item.title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
item.description: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its capital expenditures jumped nearly seven times from a year ago. Revenue also rose.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: In its first earnings report as a public company, SpaceX also posted a quarterly loss of $541 million, narrower than the $1 billion loss in the same period a year ago.

item.title: In Lawsuit, NJ Accuses Amazon of Suppressing Pay for Delivery Drivers
item.description: The state attorney general said in an antitrust lawsuit filed on Tuesday that the company was abusing its market power to keep its delivery costs low.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:description: Amazon said the lawsuit wrongly characterized the company’s activities, and that its contractor delivery partners were free to operate as they saw fit.

item.title: White House Whipsaws Silicon Valley (and Itself) Over A.I. Rules
item.description: The Trump administration has struggled with how to approach “open source” models, which are freely available to download and favored by Chinese companies.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Ana Swanson and Kate Conger
item.media:description: Chinese open-source artificial models like Kimi, made by Moonshot AI, have added a new and urgent dimension to the fight between Washington and Beijing over who will control critical technologies.

item.title: What Are Companies Getting for All That A.I. Spending?
item.description: A new field of “tokenomics” has emerged to measure the return on all the money companies are pouring into artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Lydia DePillis

item.title: Trump White House Readies AI Framework to Review Security Risks
item.description: The voluntary review process will cover closed-source artificial intelligence models, but exclude those that publish the underlying code.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Kate Conger and Ana Swanson
item.media:description: President Trump at the G7 summit with Sam Altman of OpenAI in June. The Trump administration laid out how the federal government plans to review whether new A.I. tools pose a security risk.

item.title: Man’s Claim That Brakes Failed on Jaguar Was Scam to Avoid Car Payments, Court Rules
item.description: Nathan Owen called the police, saying he was trapped in a runaway car. A judge determined it was a lie and sentenced him to more than four years in prison.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mather

item.title: A SpaceX Rocket Will Soon Crash Into the Moon
item.description: The second stage of a Falcon 9 rocket, which sent two private landers to the moon last year, will collide with the moon early Wednesday morning.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying two private lunar landers launched in January last year. The second stage of this rocket will hit the moon at 5,400 miles per hour on Wednesday.

item.title: SpaceX’s Stock Lockup Is Expiring. Prepare for a Bumpy Ride.
item.description: On Thursday, employees and other insiders at Elon Musk’s rocket company will be released from their first stock “lockup” and can start selling some of their shares.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac

item.title: If You Can’t Beat A.I., Outdress It, Tech Firms and Their Swag Say
item.description: Over the years, tech workers have proudly worn nerdy company-branded gear. But this generation of hot companies is getting fancy with its merch.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith
item.media:credit: Sam Bush for The New York Times

item.title: Google Earth Disables A.I. Tool After One Day Over Disinformation Concerns
item.description: A new Google Earth tool allowed the creation of A.I. deepfake maps. The company quickly pulled it back after users noted there were no safeguards to prevent content that could be harmful.
item.dc:creator: Adeel Hassan
item.media:description: A screenshot of Google’s announcement on Thursday about Nano Banana 2, an artificial intelligence feature.

item.title: Open Model Wars + Claire Stapleton’s Dishy Google Memoir + Substack’s Slop Fight
item.description: “It just seems like the temperature is rising on Silicon Valley.”
item.dc:creator: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Rowan Niemisto, Chris Wood and Alyssa Moxley

item.title: Five Takeaways From the Times Investigation Into Larry Ellison’s A.I. Gamble
item.description: The billionaire’s company took on ominous loads of debt to build data centers around the world. The implications go far beyond Oracle.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Mahler, Jim Rutenberg and Kirsten Grind
item.media:description: Larry Ellison spoke at the first news conference of the second Trump administration, where the president called him the “C.E.O. of everything.”

item.title: We All Do Errands. Noah Blau Films Them.
item.description: Fighting a traffic ticket. Hanging a curtain. Installing an air-conditioner. With his cult-hit online series, Noah Blau has made the mundane fascinating.
item.dc:creator: Alex Vadukul
item.media:credit: Lanna Apisukh for The New York Times
item.media:description: Noah Blau, the creator of the online video series “Errands,” and Aitana Doyle, an actress, on the streets of Bushwick in Brooklyn, during the making of a recent episode.

item.title: Larry Ellison Bet It All on the A.I. Boom. Will He Be the Face of the A.I. Bubble?
item.description: Inside the 81-year-old billionaire’s risky, debt-fueled scramble to transform his data empire into an A.I. juggernaut.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Mahler, Jim Rutenberg and Kirsten Grind

item.title: What You Need to Know About Installing Plug-In Solar Panels
item.description: You can now buy panels that plug into electrical outlets, but there are some important safety issues to consider when picking and installing a system.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Patrick Junker for The New York Times
item.media:description: Plug-in solar panels are as large as windows, and in Germany they are often installed on balconies.

item.title: The German Auto Industry, a Pillar of the National Psyche, Is Trembling
item.description: The country’s iconic carmakers are struggling with tariffs, the growth of electric vehicles and intense competition from Chinese companies.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing and Jim Tankersley
item.media:credit: Silas/Stein, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The new Mercedes-Benz S-Class at the celebration of the company’s 140th anniversary. Carl Benz filed a patent for a car in 1886.

item.title: Plug-In Solar Panels Are Starting to Sprout in U.S. Backyards
item.description: Ten U.S. states have legalized systems that can be plugged into standard wall outlets. The technology typically does not require permits or electricians.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Poppy Lynch for The New York Times
item.media:description: Alex Ottoboni with his balcony solar panel at his condo in the San Francisco Bay Area

item.title: How the Pro-Trump Media Ecosystem Is Splintering Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: Once united in support of President Trump, right-wing influencers are embroiled in feuds and losing viewers, creating a problem for Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson

item.title: Anthropic Says Its A.I. Systems Broke Into Computers at 3 Organizations
item.description: The disclosure followed OpenAI’s report last week that its own artificial intelligence had hacked into the network of an online library.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac and Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: A lectern bearing the logo of Anthropic, which did not disclose the identity of the organizations that its artificial intelligence systems had breached.

item.title: Why an A.I. Bubble Might Not Be a Bad Thing
item.description: As fears spread over a possible artificial intelligence bubble, some tech investors say: Bring it on.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith

item.title: Apple’s Profit Is Up 27%, but Expectations for Current Quarter Disappoint
item.description: The company recently raised prices on a number of products because of component supply shortages caused by the artificial intelligence boom.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang
item.media:description: Apple regained its spot as the world’s most valuable publicly traded company this week.

item.title: Big Tech’s A.I. Spending Keeps Rising. So Do the Jitters.
item.description: Amazon joined a procession of tech giants that ramped up their spending on artificial intelligence, as its capital expenditures soared 69 percent. Concerns over the industry’s spending are mounting.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Christie Hemm Klok for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta’s Eagle Mountain Data Center in Utah. Meta, Amazon, Google and Microsoft are expected to spend $1.5 trillion building data centers through next year.

item.title: U.S. Government Mislabels Map of African Countries at AIDS Conference
item.description: Nigeria, a coastal country in western Africa, was landlocked in the Sahara, among other errors. The department said it had been “hastily altered.”
item.dc:creator: Remy Tumin
item.category: President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief
United States Agency for International Development
item.media:description: A map presented by the State Department at AIDS 2026, a conference in Brazil this week.

item.title: Mistaken Username Sent Man to Prison for 18 Months, Court Finds
item.description: An appeals court in Canada acquitted Brandon Klayme of charges related to child sexual abuse imagery. His Kik username had one less underscore than another account that was involved.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:credit: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press, via ZUMA Press
item.media:description: The Nova Scotia provincial flag. Prosecutors in Nova Scotia acknowledged the conviction had been flawed.

item.title: Apple’s Siri Got an A.I. Brain Transplant. Try These 5 Prompts to Get Acclimated.
item.description: An upgrade transformed the beleaguered virtual assistant into a modern chatbot. It’s imperfect but worth trying.
item.dc:creator: Brian X. Chen

item.title: A Bay Area Pastor Made an A.I. Twin to Talk About God at Any Time
item.description: To meet the growing needs of his congregation, Justin Lester created an A.I. duplicate of himself. Every day he sees more people using it.
item.dc:creator: Eli Saslow and Erin Schaff

item.title: When A.I. Invaded ‘Heated Rivalry’ Fan Fiction, the Meltdown Was Epic
item.description: An anonymous X account posted a detailed breakdown of chatbot text in 38 popular stories inspired by the hockey romance. The fandom spiraled.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin

item.title: Microsoft Increases Spending on A.I. as Profit Jumps 31%
item.description: Like other big technology companies, Microsoft is hoping its aggressive spending on artificial intelligence is starting to translate into revenue.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:description: The Microsoft Experience Center in Manhattan on Wednesday, when Microsoft reported quarterly capital expenditures of $41 billion.

item.title: Meta’s Profit Falls 14 Percent as A.I. Spending Continues
item.description: The Silicon Valley company’s costs rose more steeply than revenue growth, as it continues to invest heavily in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Russia Charges Telegram’s Founder Pavel Durov With Facilitating Terrorism
item.description: The case against Pavel Durov reflected an ongoing fight over one of the world’s most popular messaging and media apps, which is widely used in the country.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Nechepurenko and Adam Satariano
item.media:description: Pavel Durov, left, founder of Telegram, in Paris in 2025. The Kremlin has used various methods to try to restrict access to Telegram in Russia.
